Figure 1:Geometry-native world generation.Given a reference image, a camera trajectory, and optional text, GAE jointly generates RGB views and 3D geometry froma shared, compact latent space.
Each example pairs generated RGB and depth sequences with the resulting
3D point cloud.

Figure 2:Overview of Geometry-Native Autoencoder (GAE).Stage 1 (codec training)compresses frozen multi-level geometry
foundation features into a compact, diffusable geometry latent; the feature
decoder rebuilds the full hierarchy for frozen geometry readout, while a
separate learned head decodes RGB.Stage 2 (flow training)performs
conditional flow matching only over generated-view latents, while clean
reference latents, camera rays, and text act as controls.

Figure 4:Qualitative RGB comparison on RealEstate10K.Columns are methods and rows show one reference and two target views for each
scene under identical camera conditioning. Insets report per-scene PSNR over
the two displayed target views; Ours denotes theC=64C{=}64model.

Figure 5:Independent 3D check across latent families.The appearance-native Wan2.1 VAE, semantic-native RAEv2, and geometry-native
GAE are conditioned on the same reference image and prescribed camera
trajectory. Generated views, detail crops, VGGT-reconstructed point clouds,
and recovered camera trajectories highlight the impact of the latent
representation on cross-view visual consistency and camera control.

Figure 6:Multi-frame RGB, geometry, and camera-pose comparison across
RealEstate10K scenes.Gen3R, GLD, and Ours receive the same reference image and prescribed camera
trajectory. For each scene, early, middle, and final generated views are
paired with the generated point cloud and recovered pose. The multi-scene
comparison exposes cross-frame structure, depth-layer distortions, and
trajectory drift that are less apparent in a single final view.

Figure 7:Long-rollout showcase.Five views from each 81-view rollout and the point cloud decoded from the same
latents.

Figure 8:Text-conditioned RGB and geometry generation.Each pair shows an RGB sample and depth decoded from the same latent. These
selected examples demonstrate capability rather than benchmark text-to-image
quality.

Figure 9:Independent 3D check of generated views.The appearance-native WAN2.1 VAE, semantic-native RAEV2, and our
geometry-native latent receive the same reference and camera controls. The
right-hand panels show point clouds and camera trajectories reconstructed from
the generated RGB clips by an independent geometry model VGGT.

Figure 10:RealEstate10K comparison.All methods receive the same reference image and target camera trajectory, and
the eight remaining views are generated jointly.

Figure 11:DL3DV comparison.All methods receive the same reference image and target camera trajectory, and
the eight remaining views are generated jointly.
